fragment_A.why: Five declared, four recorded, none false. The verdict follows from the absent assertion — NOT from re-deriving it against response.body.data.total_cents (500). Re-derivation is acquisition, it is unavailable for side-effect assertions, and an evaluator that does it here will do it where it has no evidence to do it with.

fragment_B.why: A conformant bundle of a failing scenario: all five results present, one false. Same verdict as fragment A, entirely different event — a product defect with a complete record versus an incomplete record.

harness_findings.detail: Both skipped assertions would have been false against the recorded response. The report cannot distinguish 'one thing is broken' from 'at least one thing is broken and we stopped counting'.

fragment_C.why: The verdict is right and the run is defective. Steps 6-8 never short-circuit: the cost is a few wasted probes on a doomed scenario, the benefit is that one failing run reports everything that is wrong.

conformance_note: An evaluator that reads only the bundle cannot pass fragments A or C — it has no way to know five assertions were declared. Check that structurally before running anything: if the evaluator's signature does not take the specification, it is non-conformant by construction.
